cluster_summary: The majority of these vulnerabilities stem from using untrusted user input (e.g., sort column names, order fields, filter parameters) directly in SQL or HQL queries without allow-list validation, enabling injection. One case has a validation timing flaw, two involve incomplete structural validation of HQL queries, one misses a configuration check for sorting obfuscated fields, and one is an algorithmic complexity issue unrelated to injection.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Conditionally disable sorting on the obfuscated field by checking the configuration flag before building the HQL sort clause..
